_help: Story structures for the videos (ideas.py; owner 2026-10-27: 'go ahead': stories instead of feature lists). Each project of the strategist's sheet names one (`structure`) or invents one (`structure` id of its own + `structure_name` + `shape`); every chapter names its `beat`. A structure is used once a batch and not by the product's last batch. beats: in order; required ones must be there; pace sets the shot length of that beat's chapter (slow ~2.4 s, normal ~1.9 s, fast ~1.6 s); a `proof_shot` chapter is one beat where the picture proves the line: its shot is held 2-3 s and plays the clip's own sound (a zip closing). The offer is always the last chapter (beat `offer`), the only place with the price.
rules: One promise per video and at most 3 features; each video of the batch leads with a different feature.

Set the story where the footage is: the packet's place tags with many moments (street, home, car, cafe, office ...). A place the library never filmed (a train platform, an airport) only reads as a street, so say it lightly or pick another.
The price, the %, the sale and the bundle are said only in the last chapter (and in at most one hook).
Every video has one proof shot (two at most): a chapter with `proof_shot: true` whose `show` tags are a movement (zip, side_zip, zip_hand, snap, lock, pocket, packing, strap, tie).

The four hooks open on four different pictures of the bag doing something (their first `show` tag a movement or a person, never hero / placed / colours), and they raise a question or show a moment; the price hook at most once.
People: a project without the presenter shows the bag on a person (worn / walking) in at least two chapters; the voice talks like a friend, in 'you' form.
No invented customer, no first person, no claim the packet's facts do not hold.

structures.name: One moment
structures.shape: A single real situation told in the present tense, start to finish: where you are, the small problem of that moment, what the bag does about it, how the moment ends. No list.

beats.says: where and when, in one or two short sentences
the small problem of this moment
what the bag does about it (the main feature)
a second small thing it handles (optional)
the offer, ending 'Tap the link below.'

structures.example: Six-fifteen, the platform is packed. -> Your card is in the hidden pocket on the back, tap and it's back before the gates close. -> Home, keys exactly where you left them.

structures.name: A test, live
structures.shape: One challenge done on camera and counted or timed: the one-hand test, how many things fit, how fast the strap switches. The proof is the test itself.

beats.says: the feature that made it work

structures.example: Can you open it with one hand? -> One pull on the side zip, phone out. -> Done, the other hand never let go of the coffee.

structures.name: Myth vs fact
structures.shape: A belief people hold about bags, said, then turned around with what the bag shows. Calm, not preachy.

beats.says: the belief (big bags are messy, secure bags look dull, crossbodies are for tourists)

structures.example: Big bags turn into a black hole. -> Not when the inside is divided. -> Keys in one place, phone in another, nothing sinks.

structures.name: Gift reveal
structures.shape: The moment a gift is opened, for one named person (mum, a sister, a best friend), and the two reasons it suits her. Warm, slow.

beats.says: who it is for and what her days are like
the first reason it suits her

structures.example: For the mum who carries everyone's things. -> Out of the tissue paper, soft and zipped. -> Room for all of it, and it still looks good at dinner.

structures.name: Advice to a friend
structures.shape: A friend's situation ('your sister is flying to Rome next week') and the advice you would give her about the bag, in 'you' form. Never 'I' or 'my'.
structures.example: Your sister is flying to Rome next week. -> Tell her to take a bag that zips shut. -> Passport in the back pocket, flat against her.

structures.name: Four places, one bag
structures.shape: One day in four short places (the train, the office, the cafe, the evening), one small moment each, the same bag throughout.

beats.says: the fourth place, the day ends

structures.example: 8 am, the train. -> 11, the office: phone in the side zip. -> 1, the cafe. -> 7, dinner, the strap off, a handbag again.

structures.name: What you carry now
structures.shape: The bag you carry now (an open tote, no brand named, never shown as bad) next to this one: two differences you can see, then the switch.

beats.says: the bag you carry now and its one problem

structures.example: Your tote is open at the top. -> This one zips shut. -> One pull, and nothing is on show.

structures.name: POV
structures.shape: 'POV: ...' a second-person scene the viewer steps into ('POV: you're boarding in twenty minutes'), told beat by beat until it resolves.

beats.says: the POV line: where you are

structures.example: POV: you're boarding in twenty minutes. -> Passport? Back pocket. -> Phone? Side zip. -> Seat 14C, nothing dug for.

structures.name: The night before
structures.shape: Packing the bag the night before something (a trip, a first day, a wedding): what goes where, the zip closing, the morning after.

beats.says: the morning: grab it and go

structures.example: Tomorrow is the wedding. -> Lipstick, cards, phone, each in its place. -> Zipped. -> Morning: grab it and go.
